title_en: Provisional Regulations of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Justice, and the Ministry of Health on Judicial Assessment of Mental Illness
full_text_en:
Provisional Regulations of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Justice, and the Ministry of Health on Forensic Psychiatric Evaluation

Document No. Wei Yi Zi (89) No. 17

Chapter I General Provisions

Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (For Trial Implementation), the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Administrative Penalties for Public Security, and other relevant laws and regulations, for the purpose of enabling judicial organs to handle cases correctly according to law and protecting the lawful rights and interests of persons suffering from mental diseases.

Article 2 Forensic psychiatric evaluation shall, based on the facts of the case and the mental state of the subject of evaluation, produce an expert conclusion, providing scientific evidence on relevant legal capacity to the entrusting evaluation organ.

Chapter II Forensic Psychiatric Evaluation Institutions

Article 3 To carry out the work of forensic psychiatric evaluation, provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government, prefectures, and prefecture-level cities shall establish forensic psychiatric evaluation committees, which shall be responsible for reviewing and approving evaluators, organizing technical evaluation groups, coordinating and carrying out evaluation work.

Article 4 An evaluation committee shall be composed of relevant responsible cadres and experts from the people's courts, people's procuratorates, and the public security, judicial, and health organs. The candidates shall be determined through consultation among the said organs.

Article 5 An evaluation committee may, as needed, establish several technical evaluation groups to undertake specific evaluation work. Members of such groups shall be engaged or appointed by the evaluation committee. No technical evaluation group shall have fewer than two members participating in the evaluation.

Article 6 For difficult cases that cannot be evaluated within a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, the entrusting evaluation organ may re-entrust the evaluation committee of another province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government to conduct the evaluation.

Chapter III Scope of Evaluation

Article 7 Evaluation shall be conducted on the following persons who may be suffering from a mental disease:
(1) Defendants and victims in criminal cases;
(2) Parties in civil cases;
(3) Plaintiffs (natural persons) in administrative cases;
(4) Persons who have violated public security administration and are subject to detention punishment;
(5) Criminals undergoing reform through labor;
(6) Persons undergoing re-education through labor;
(7) Persons under custody for investigation;
(8) Other persons related to the case who need evaluation.

Article 8 The evaluation committee may, depending on the circumstances, accept requests from the subject of evaluation for supplementary evaluation, re-evaluation, or review evaluation.

Article 9 In criminal cases, forensic psychiatric evaluation includes:
(1) Determining whether the subject of evaluation suffers from a mental disease, what type of mental disease, the mental state at the time of committing the harmful act, the relationship between the mental disease and the harmful act committed, and whether the subject has criminal responsibility.
(2) Determining the mental state of the subject during the litigation process and whether the subject has capacity to participate in litigation.
(3) Determining the mental state of the subject during the period of serving a sentence and making recommendations on legal measures to be taken.

Article 10 In civil cases, the tasks of forensic psychiatric evaluation are as follows:
(1) Determining whether the subject of evaluation suffers from a mental disease, what type of mental disease, the mental state when engaging in civil activities, the influence of the mental disease on the subject's ability to express intentions, and whether the subject has capacity for civil conduct.
(2) Determining the mental state of the subject during the mediation or trial phase and whether the subject has capacity to participate in litigation.

Article 11 Determining the mental state of victims and others in various types of cases at the time their lawful rights and interests such as personal and property rights are infringed upon, and whether they have the ability to recognize the infringing act or the ability to defend or protect themselves.

Article 12 Determining the mental state of relevant witnesses in a case and whether they have capacity to testify.

Chapter IV Evaluators

Article 13 Persons who possess one of the following qualifications may serve as evaluators:
(1) Persons at the level of attending physician or above who have more than five years of clinical psychiatric experience and possess knowledge of forensic psychiatry.
(2) Persons at the level of chief forensic physician or above who possess knowledge, experience, and working ability in forensic psychiatry.

Article 14 Rights of Evaluators
(1) Where the case materials concerning the subject of evaluation are insufficient, the evaluator may request the entrusting evaluation organ to provide the necessary case materials.
(2) The evaluator has the right, through the entrusting evaluation organ, to obtain information from the subject's work unit, relatives, and relevant witnesses.
(3) The evaluator has the right, as needed, to request the entrusting evaluation organ to transfer the subject of evaluation to a hospital that admits and treats mental patients for inpatient examination and evaluation.
(4) The evaluation institution may inquire of the entrusting evaluation organ about the handling of the case after the evaluation.

Article 15 Obligations of Evaluators
(1) When conducting an evaluation, the evaluator shall perform duties and produce an expert conclusion correctly and promptly.
(2) Answer questions raised by the entrusting evaluation organ that are related to the expert conclusion.
(3) Maintain the confidentiality of the case.
(4) Comply with legal provisions concerning withdrawal.

Article 16 If an evaluator engages in malpractice for personal gain or intentionally makes a false evaluation during the evaluation process, legal liability shall be pursued.

Chapter V Entrustment of Evaluation and the Evaluation Report

Article 17 When a judicial organ entrusts an evaluation, it shall provide a "Letter of Entrustment for Evaluation," specifying the requirements and purpose of the evaluation, and shall provide the following materials:
(1) Information on the subject of evaluation and the subject's family situation;
(2) Relevant materials of the case;
(3) Relevant materials provided by the subject's work unit;
(4) Testimony from persons who know the subject's mental state;
(5) Medical records and other relevant examination results.

Article 18 After the evaluation is completed, an "Evaluation Report" shall be prepared.
The "Evaluation Report" shall include the following contents:
(1) The name of the entrusting evaluation organ;
(2) The cause of action, case number, and evaluation report number;
(3) The purpose and requirements of the evaluation;
(4) The date and place of the evaluation, and persons present;
(5) A summary of the case;
(6) General information on the subject of evaluation;
(7) The mental state of the subject of evaluation at the time of the incident and during various stages before and after the incident;
(8) Findings from the mental state examination and other examinations of the subject of evaluation;
(9) Analysis and explanation;
(10) Expert conclusion;
(11) Signatures of the evaluators and affixing the special seal for evaluation;
(12) Recommendations regarding medical treatment or guardianship.

Chapter VI Assessment of Responsibility and Capacity

Article 19 Assessment of the criminal responsibility of the subject of evaluation in criminal cases:
Where, at the time of committing the harmful act, the subject of evaluation is determined through evaluation to be suffering from a mental disease, and due to severe disturbance of mental activity is unable to recognize or control his/her own conduct, the subject shall be found to have no criminal responsibility.
Where, at the time of committing the harmful act, the subject of evaluation is determined through evaluation to fall under one of the following circumstances, the subject shall be found to have criminal responsibility:
1. Having a past history of mental disease but no mental abnormality at the time of committing the harmful act;
2. Being in a remission period of mental disease with all psychiatric symptoms having completely disappeared.

Article 20 Assessment of the capacity for civil conduct of the subject of evaluation in civil cases:
(1) Where, at the time of engaging in civil activities, the subject of evaluation is determined through evaluation to be suffering from a mental disease, and due to severe disturbance of mental activity is unable to recognize or unable to protect his/her own lawful rights and interests, the subject shall be found to have no capacity for civil conduct.
(2) Where, at the time of engaging in civil activities, the subject of evaluation is determined through evaluation to be suffering from a mental disease, and due to disturbance of mental activity is unable to fully recognize, unable to control, or unable to fully protect his/her own lawful rights and interests, the subject shall be found to have limited capacity for civil conduct.
(3) Where, at the time of engaging in civil activities, the subject of evaluation is determined through evaluation to fall under one of the following circumstances, the subject shall be found to have capacity for civil conduct:
1. Having a past history of mental disease but no mental abnormality at the time of the civil activities;
2. Being in a remission period of mental disease with all psychiatric symptoms having completely disappeared;
3. Although suffering from a mental disease, the pathological mental activity has significant limitations, and the subject has the ability to recognize and to protect his/her own lawful rights and interests in relation to the civil activities engaged in;
4. Having low intelligence but still having the ability to recognize and protect his/her own lawful rights and interests.

Article 21 Assessment of relevant legal capacity during litigation:
(1) Where the subject of evaluation is a defendant in a criminal case and, during the litigation process, is determined through evaluation to be suffering from a mental disease such that he/she is unable to exercise procedural rights, the subject shall be found to have no capacity to participate in litigation.
(2) Where the subject of evaluation is a party in a civil case or a private prosecutor in a criminal case and, during the litigation process, is determined through evaluation to be suffering from a mental disease such that he/she is unable to exercise procedural rights, the subject shall be found to have no capacity to participate in litigation.
(3) Where an accuser, informant, witness, or other person provides testimony inconsistent with the facts and is determined through evaluation to be suffering from a mental disease such that he/she lacks the ability to understand or judge objective facts, the subject shall be found to have no capacity to testify.

Article 22 Assessment of other relevant legal capacity:
(1) Where the subject of evaluation is female and is determined through evaluation to be suffering from a mental disease, and at the time her right to sexual inviolability is infringed upon, she lacks the ability to substantially understand the infringement suffered or the serious consequences thereof, she shall be found to have no capacity for self-defense.
(2) Where the subject of evaluation, while serving a sentence, undergoing re-education through labor, or being subject to public security penalties, is determined through evaluation to be suffering from a mental disease, and due to severe disturbance of mental activity lacks the ability to recognize or control conduct, the subject shall be found to have no capacity to serve the sentence, undergo re-education through labor, or bear the penalty.

Chapter VII Supplementary Provisions

Article 23 These Regulations shall take effect as of August 1, 1989.

July 11, 1989
